NIS2-A3.title: Registration with the national authority
NIS2-A3.statement: Register with the competent authority, providing name, contact details, IP ranges, sector and subsector, and the list of Member States where services covered by the directive are provided. Any change must be reported within two weeks.

requirements.NIS2-A3-R1: Determine its category (essential or important entity) and its sector.
requirements.NIS2-A3-R2: Provide name, address, up-to-date contact details, IP ranges and sector to the competent authority.
requirements.NIS2-A3-R3: Declare the Member States in which services covered by the directive are provided.
requirements.NIS2-A3-R4: Report any change within two weeks at most.

NIS2-A3.deadline: Two weeks to report any change
evidence: Entity identity sheet kept up to date

NIS2-A20.chapter: Chapter IV: Cybersecurity risk-management measures and reporting obligations
NIS2-A20.title: Governance and accountability of management bodies
NIS2-A20.statement: Have risk-management measures approved by the management body, have it oversee their implementation, and train its members. This is the provision that makes managers personally accountable: breaches of Article 21 can be attributed to them, and the authority may go as far as banning them from management functions.

requirements.NIS2-A20-R1: Have the management body formally approve risk-management measures, and record this approval.
requirements.NIS2-A20-R2: Organise periodic oversight of implementation at management level.
requirements.NIS2-A20-R3: Have members of the management body follow cybersecurity training.
requirements.NIS2-A20-R4: Extend equivalent training to staff on a regular basis.

NIS2-A20.deadline: Periodic approval and review, regular training
evidence: Monitoring dashboard presented to the executive committee

NIS2-A21-1.title: Appropriate, proportionate, risk-based measures
NIS2-A21-1.statement: Take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage the risks posed to network and information systems, and to limit the impact of incidents on service recipients. Proportionality is assessed against exposure, size and the likely severity of incidents.

requirements.NIS2-A21-1-R1: Inventory the activities, services and information systems that contribute to their delivery.
requirements.NIS2-A21-1-R2: Justify the level of measures chosen in light of exposure, size and criticality.
requirements.NIS2-A21-1-R3: Adopt an all-hazards approach that also covers the physical environment.

evidence: Map of activities, services and systems

NIS2-A21-2a.title: Risk analysis and information system security policies
NIS2-A21-2a.statement: Have a risk analysis policy and an information system security policy that are formalised, approved and applied. The ReCyF makes them the foundation: without this documentary framework, no other objective can be demonstrated.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2a-R1: Formalise an information security policy covering encryption, physical and logical access control, and review of measures.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2a-R2: Define a risk analysis method and apply it to the inventoried systems.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2a-R3: Set up and track an action plan closing the gaps identified.

evidence: Dated and approved information security policy

NIS2-A21-2b.title: Incident handling
NIS2-A21-2b.statement: Have a documented process for detecting, qualifying, handling and learning from security incidents, with identified roles and an alert chain operating around the clock.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2b-R1: Define an incident management procedure with qualification and severity criteria.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2b-R2: Assign handling roles and organise 24/7 coverage of the alert chain.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2b-R3: Log every incident and carry out a lessons-learned review.

NIS2-A21-2c.title: Business continuity, backups and crisis management
NIS2-A21-2c.statement: Have a continuity and recovery set-up based on tested backups, defined recovery objectives, and a formalised and exercised crisis organisation.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2c-R1: Define maximum tolerable downtime and data recovery points.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2c-R2: Keep backups isolated from production systems and test their restoration.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2c-R3: Formalise a cyber crisis management set-up, with backup communication means.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2c-R4: Exercise the crisis set-up at a defined frequency.

NIS2-A21-2c.deadline: Periodic restoration tests and crisis exercises

NIS2-A21-2d.title: Supply chain security
NIS2-A21-2d.statement: Address the security of relationships with direct suppliers and service providers, taking into account each one's specific vulnerabilities, the overall quality of their cybersecurity practices and their secure development procedures. Article 21(3) also requires taking into account coordinated risk assessments carried out at EU level.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2d-R1: Map the ecosystem of suppliers and service providers and rate their criticality.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2d-R2: Assess the specific vulnerabilities of each direct supplier and the quality of its practices.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2d-R3: Include security requirements in contracts and check they are applied.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2d-R4: Take into account the results of coordinated risk assessments for critical supply chains (Art. 22).

evidence: Map of suppliers and their criticality

NIS2-A21-2e.title: Security in acquisition, development and maintenance
NIS2-A21-2e.statement: Build security into the acquisition, development and maintenance of systems, including vulnerability handling and disclosure. This covers in-house development as well as off-the-shelf purchases.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2e-R1: Define security requirements for acquisitions and developments.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2e-R2: Control changes: qualification, validation and reversibility.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2e-R3: Organise monitoring, handling and patching of vulnerabilities within defined time frames.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2e-R4: Provide a coordinated vulnerability disclosure channel.

NIS2-A21-2f.title: Assessing the effectiveness of measures
NIS2-A21-2f.statement: Have policies and procedures to assess the actual effectiveness of risk-management measures, not just their existence. This is where documentary compliance stops being enough.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2f-R1: Define effectiveness indicators and a measurement frequency.
NIS2-A21-2f-R2: Carry out security audits and address the gaps found.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2f-R3: Report the results to the management body.

NIS2-A21-2g.title: Cyber hygiene and cybersecurity training
NIS2-A21-2g.statement: Put in place basic cyber hygiene practices and a cybersecurity training programme covering all users, including service providers acting on the entity's behalf.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2g-R1: Define rules for using IT resources and communicate them to users.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2g-R2: Organise regular awareness sessions adapted to profiles and risks.

NIS2-A21-2h.title: Cryptography and encryption
NIS2-A21-2h.statement: Define and apply policies and procedures on the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption, which requires a key and algorithm management policy, not just turning on encryption in transit.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2h-R1: Define a cryptography policy: algorithms, key lengths, use cases.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2h-R2: Manage the life cycle of keys and certificates.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2h-R3: Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in transit according to the policy.

NIS2-A21-2i.title: Human resources security, access control and asset management
NIS2-A21-2i.statement: Manage security across the people life cycle (joining, moving, leaving), apply a need-to-know access control policy, and keep an asset inventory.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2i-R1: Formalise joiner, mover and leaver procedures, including removal of access.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2i-R2: Apply least privilege and periodically review granted rights.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2i-R3: Separate and specifically protect administration accounts.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2i-R4: Keep an inventory of hardware and software assets and assign owners.

NIS2-A21-2j.title: Multi-factor authentication and secure communications
NIS2-A21-2j.statement: Use, where appropriate, multi-factor or continuous authentication, secured voice, video and text communications, and secured emergency communication systems within the entity.

requirements.NIS2-A21-2j-R1: Deploy multi-factor authentication on remote access and privileged accounts.
requirements.NIS2-A21-2j-R3: Provide an emergency communication means independent of the everyday information system.

evidence: Description of the backup communication means

NIS2-A21-4.title: Corrective measures when non-compliance is found
NIS2-A21-4.statement: When the entity itself finds that it does not comply with the measures of paragraph 2, take all necessary, appropriate and proportionate corrective measures without undue delay.

requirements.NIS2-A21-4-R1: Organise internal detection of compliance gaps.
requirements.NIS2-A21-4-R2: Record each gap, its correction plan and its due date.

NIS2-A21-4.deadline: Without undue delay once the gap is found
evidence: Gap register and related action plan

NIS2-A23-1.title: Notification of significant incidents to the CSIRT
NIS2-A23-1.statement: Notify without undue delay any incident with a significant impact on service provision. An incident is significant if it has caused or may cause severe operational disruption or financial loss, or has affected others by causing considerable damage.

requirements.NIS2-A23-1-R1: Define internal criteria for qualifying a significant incident.
requirements.NIS2-A23-1-R2: Identify the point of contact and the notification channel with the national CSIRT.
requirements.NIS2-A23-1-R3: Provide the information needed to assess cross-border impact.

NIS2-A23-1.deadline: Without undue delay after becoming aware of the incident
guidance: Technical implementation guidance on NIS2 measures

NIS2-A23-4.title: Reporting sequence: 24 hours, 72 hours, one month
NIS2-A23-4.statement: Follow the three-step sequence: an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notification within 72 hours, then a final report no later than one month after that notification. Trust service providers have a single 24-hour deadline.

requirements.NIS2-A23-4-R1: Send an early warning within 24 hours, indicating any suspected malicious cause and cross-border impact.
requirements.NIS2-A23-4-R2: Send within 72 hours an initial assessment of severity, impact and indicators of compromise.
requirements.NIS2-A23-4-R3: Produce an intermediate report at the request of the CSIRT or authority.
requirements.NIS2-A23-4-R4: Submit a final report within one month: detailed description, root cause, mitigation measures, cross-border impact.
requirements.NIS2-A23-4-R5: If the incident is still ongoing, provide a progress report and then the final report one month after closure.

NIS2-A23-2.title: Informing service recipients
NIS2-A23-2.statement: Inform service recipients without undue delay of significant incidents likely to affect the provision of those services, and tell them what measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat.

requirements.NIS2-A23-2-R1: Identify the recipients to inform and the communication channels.
requirements.NIS2-A23-2-R2: Prepare incident and cyber threat communication templates.

NIS2-A24.title: Use of European certification schemes
NIS2-A24.statement: Member States may require the use of products, services or processes certified under a European cybersecurity certification scheme. Absent such a requirement, certification remains a way to demonstrate compliance.

requirements.NIS2-A24-R1: Check whether a national certification requirement exists for the sector.
requirements.NIS2-A24-R2: Where applicable, favour qualified or certified products and services.

evidence: List of qualified products and services selected

NIS2-A26.title: Determining jurisdiction
NIS2-A26.statement: Determine the competent Member State: in principle the one of establishment, but for digital service providers and managed service providers, the one of the main establishment, meaning where cybersecurity risk-management decisions are mainly taken.

requirements.NIS2-A26-R1: Identify the competent Member State and the relevant authority.
requirements.NIS2-A26-R2: Designate a representative in the Union if the entity is not established there.

NIS2-A27.title: European registry of digital providers
NIS2-A27.statement: DNS service providers, domain name registries, providers of cloud computing, data centres, content delivery networks, managed and managed security services, as well as online marketplaces, search engines and social networks, submit their identification details, centralised by ENISA.

requirements.NIS2-A27-R1: Submit name, sector, type of entity, main establishment address and contact details.
requirements.NIS2-A27-R2: Declare the Member States in which services are provided.
requirements.NIS2-A27-R3: Update this information without delay when it changes.

evidence: Confirmation of submission to the competent authority

NIS2-A30.title: Information sharing and voluntary notification
NIS2-A30.statement: Take part, on a voluntary basis, in threat information-sharing arrangements, and report incidents or near misses that fall outside the notification obligation. A voluntary notification creates no additional obligation.

requirements.NIS2-A30-R1: Assess whether to join a sectoral sharing arrangement.
requirements.NIS2-A30-R2: Define internal rules for sharing sensitive information.

evidence: Membership of a sectoral sharing arrangement

NIS2-A32.title: Being ready for supervisory measures
NIS2-A32.statement: Essential entities are subject to ex ante supervision: on-site inspections, security audits at their own expense, requests for evidence, security scans. Important entities are subject to ex post supervision, triggered by evidence of a breach. This difference in regime is the heaviest practical consequence of the categorisation.

requirements.NIS2-A32-R1: Keep compliance evidence immediately available and up to date.
requirements.NIS2-A32-R2: Be able to respond to an audit or inspection request.
NIS2-A32-R3: Plan for funding audits requested by the authority.
